designSummary: Descriptive audit of all eligible incidents against the standard; no comparative inference unless outcome data become available.
sampleSize: All eligible incidents are included: about 450 over three and a half years. If 60 percent are treated within three hours, the 95 percent confidence interval is about 4.5 percentage points either side; for single-paramedic incidents (perhaps 90) it widens to about 10 points, enough to see a gap of 20 points or more.
primaryAnalysis: Proportion treated within three hours with a Wilson 95 percent confidence interval, overall and by crew configuration, age band and transport time band, plotted by quarter.
secondaryAnalysis: Median time from injury to dose with interquartile range, separately for known and estimated injury times; reasons for not treating.
missingData: Records without an injury time are counted and reported; they enter the primary outcome only if the dose was clearly within or outside three hours of the call time.
multiplicity: Descriptive estimates only; no significance tests.
software: Spreadsheet and R for intervals and charts, kept by the audit team.
overfittingGuards: No outcome modelling without linked data
summary: About 450 incidents give a compliance estimate within about 4.5 percentage points.
